newsitem.title: UK: International bond issues to top $400 bln in H1.
newsitem.headline: International bond issues to top $400 bln in H1.

text.p: Volume of international bond issuance for the first half of 1997 is set to rise nearly 30 percent versus the same period last year, Capital DATA Bondware figures showed on Thursday.
Volumes for the half-year look set to top $400 billion, based on figures for up to June 26.
In the first half of last year, borrowers issued $315 billion in the international bond markets, 49 percent up from the same period of 1995.
International bonds worth a total of $678 billion were launched in the whole of 1996, up from the record-breaking $465 billion issued the previous year.
Dollars, marks and sterling were the most active currency sectors in 1997 so far.
The dollar sector remained top with $193 billion issued, a 49 percent market share.
Second on the ladder, mark-denominated bonds totalled almost $50 billion equivalent, or 12 percent.
Sterling came a strong third with around $41 billion, or a 10 percent market share.
Emerging market borrowers will have raised around $60 billion in the first half of 1997, the figures showed.
